citation: Chéruel (ed.), Lettres du cardinal Mazarin pendant son ministère, t. VI (Sept 1653-juin 1655), chronological table / 'Analyses des lettres' (pp. ~716-717): 29 (or 30) juin 1655, La Fère, 'A Talon, intendant d'armée', analysed only (enemy advanced to Ribemont; plan to gather troops and press them without fighting); source cited as Aff. étr., Pays-Bas t. 34, not Chantilly Ms 1485
note: Full text of the 29 Jun 1655 letter is NOT printed (one-paragraph analysis only; OCR of the table is rough, so the row is probably but not certainly the Chantilly letter). No cipher string, no decipherment. The 22 Jun and 4 Jul 1656 letters were not located in t. VII (its Talon letters come from Pays-Bas and Mélanges Colbert minutes; Ms 1485 is a Turenne recueil and is not cited). Keep open; the clear Pays-Bas minutes are a possible crib source.

citation: Berger de Xivrey & Guadet (ed.), Recueil des lettres missives de Henri IV, t. VIII (Supplément, 1872), pp. 685-691: Henri IV to Sillery, Saint-Germain-en-Laye, 13 Dec 1597 (signed Neufville); the ciphered passage is printed in clear with the remark '(Passage en chiffres.)' (p. 686)
note: Plaintext for the whole letter including the ciphered passage; no cipher string. Closed as a reading target. Date and Calais/Cardinal Albert/Père général content match the entry.

citation: Recueil des lettres missives de Henri IV, t. VIII (Supplément, 1872), pp. 779-780: Henri IV (signed Neufville/Villeroy) to Sillery, Grenoble, 14 Aug 1600, Saluces affair; the ciphered part is not given: editor writes '(suivent sept lignes chiffrées)'
note: Page is 779-780 in the OCR, not 774 as in the brief. Plain parts printed; seven cipher lines omitted and not deciphered, so they stay unread (short). Sender is Henri IV via Villeroy, not 'unknown'.

citation: Chantilly Ms 1967 = série Z t. XXXIV (Z 34). Its letters (Montgaillard, Fauche-Borel, Demougé, Mme de Reich, pp. 1-264) are cited item by item and used in deciphered form in Caudrillier, La trahison de Pichegru et les intrigues royalistes dans l'Est avant fructidor (Paris 1908); many were printed earlier in Correspondance trouvée dans les fourgons du général Klinglin (Paris, an VI, Réal's deciphered edition); Pichegru's musical-note billets survive only as decipherments (Caudrillier, introduction p. xiii)
note: Caudrillier says the Strasbourg correspondents' and Demougé's 1796 letters were sent in cipher, deciphered by Mme de Reich and the abbé Jœglé, and 'le déchiffrement de Strasbourg' agrees with Réal's printed text; the volume's front tables are that decipherment. Cipher strings are not printed in Caudrillier. Read at the time and in print, not an open cipher target. Daudet (Revue des Deux Mondes 1901) and Chantilly Ms 1988 (musical scores) not separately checked; Caudrillier says Wickham took the musical originals and only translations survive.

citation: Rommel (ed.), Correspondance inédite de Henri IV, roi de France et de Navarre, avec Maurice-le-Savant, landgrave de Hesse (Paris 1840), pp. 297-299: Maurice to Henri IV, Cassel, 28 Mar 1606 (French; regret over the Bouillon affair, Hungary, Brunswick, birth of a daughter)
note: Full plaintext printed; no cipher string and no editor's cipher note on this letter (nearby letters of 12 and 15 Mar 1606 carry notes that the originals were in chiffres). Print gives the year as '1600' (typo for 1606). Closed.

citation: Arckenholtz, Mémoires concernant Christine reine de Suède, t. III (Amsterdam 1759), section on the Polish election (pp. ~340-390): extracts and paraphrases of Père Prieur Hacki's despatches and Christina's instruction to him, from 'Negoziati di Polonia'; the dated Hacki letters (31 Oct 1668-19 Apr 1669) are not printed in full
note: Arckenholtz notes that he holds Christina's ciphers (four kinds, from Rome) and that some of her ciphered letters are undeciphered in print. His source is a Roman/Neapolitan collection, not shown to be Montpellier H 258. Extracts give context and some cribs (nuncio, Neubourg, Moscovite) but not the letters.

citation: Arckenholtz t. III, same section, reports the nuncio's views by paraphrase; the two nuncio despatches of 21 Nov 1668 and 1 May 1669 are not identified as printed
note: Weak: paraphrase only. Åkerman and published Vatican correspondence not searched.

citation: Arckenholtz t. III prints Christina's 1672 instruction for the marquis del Monte (Diet of 1672) and mentions Texeira; the four letters of 16 Jul-8 Oct 1672 were not found in t. III or t. IV text
Pusch, Donald E., 'Kerlérec's cipher: the code book of Louisiana's last French governor', Louisiana History 49, no. 4 (Fall 2008), pp. 463-480
note: Article not read (JSTOR; a Scribd copy exists, not opened). Secondary summaries say Kerlérec's code book does not survive and Pusch reconstructs the code (with C. David Lodge's software filter) and decodes letters of 1752-63, quoting e.g. the 21 Oct 1757 letter on Fort Ascension. So the code is probably solved and the 1755 despatches in C13A 39 are within its span; which despatches are given in clear is unverified. Get the article before treating 1206/1207 as open.

citation: Pusch 2008 (same article) covers Kerlérec's coded letters 1752-63, so C13A 41/42 (1759-60) fall within it; C13A 21 (1736) predates Kerlérec and is outside it
note: Unverified as above. Maggs Bros also lists a loose Dec 1756 Kerlérec cipher despatch (nomenclator, number code).
